Well, I thought I will just check how a cannon crew would look like, and then I got carried away. It was so satisfying to do these little dwarfs, that I neglected my other hobbie. I might focus on those on the weekend then instead of modeling.

So this kit includes two different carriages (different wheel variants), seven barrel alternatives (though number four is actually the original empire one), and nine crewmen. I only planned six of those, without the imperial looking ones, but - as mentioned above - I got carried away. And they already had some very nice miniatures to work with. Also most of my Warhammer cannons have those crewmen.

I also added the siege bombard accessories here as well, they fit the model perfectly, I think.

General information

My miniatures are designed to work out of the box with original 28mm Heroquest miniatures.
I always add a version with Heroquest base and one without a base. The weapons and the base are only combined (if possible).
Personally, I now prefer 32mm miniatures. I usually scale them to 112% -115% directly in the slicer.

I am happy about every shared make, especially the painted ones.
By the way i love espresso, so don't hesitate to leave a tip if you like =D

If you are inexperienced with slicer setting, I recommend this one for Ender Printer: http://www.fatdragongames.com/fdgfiles/?p=4934

This elite unit is made with experienced warriors, often the tallest and the strongest of their kind to be able to swing huge hammers into the battlefield. They wear large armors, which add to their impressive presence among a dwarven army.

To make them, I had in mind the fact that I hate the GW models showing dwarves holding hammer above their head in a strange movement which should end in the neck of the unit's front rank. I wanted to make a more worthy unit with noble and right standing, cold blooded elite fighters and not a warband with wild drunk smelly dudes.

Each model is made of four parts: body, feet on the base, hammer head and shield. The leader is the only one who has his own "feeted" base. Each body is on the same basis but with head turned and decorated differently (nude, circlet, helmet). You can add more personality to the group by turning hammer's heads on various angles. Be careful with that tip and check that your model can stack on the second rank of the unit before gluing the hammer.
I also made a standard which can take the place of a hammer's head.

Note that the models on the picture have 110% the size of the downloadable ones. I resized them after having printed my whole unit so that I'm stuck with those a little bit too tall dwarves. Yours will be better.
